## The reconstruction framework (`dynamics/reconstruct`) {#sec-ch04-framework}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md chapter 4, scheme 4.2

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Returns a left and a right state for every face of one direction, from the cell primitives.
- Two interpolants per direction: `interp1` for density and tracers, `interp2` for velocity and pressure.
- Switches: `dynamics/reconstruct/{vertical,horizontal}/{type,scale,shock}`; YAML defaults `dc`, false, false.
- With `shock: true` every row takes `interp1` and no floor is applied.
- Floors come from the equation of state, not from the reconstruct options.
:::

A reconstruction turns cell averages into the two one-sided face states a Riemann solver needs. snapy keeps two
of them per block, one for the vertical direction and one shared by the two horizontal directions, because the
vertical is the direction with an $O(1)$ background stratification and generally wants a different interpolant
from the horizontals.

The framework's own content is small but it decides three things that matter downstream: which rows take which
interpolant, where in the index range the reconstruction is allowed to write, and which floors are applied to
the result.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive about the splitting itself; it is a design choice and the code is the only record of
it. Two parts of it are worth stating plainly because they are easy to misread.

First, the rows are not treated alike. Density and tracers go through `interp1`, which is the interpolant the
user named. Velocity and pressure go through `interp2`, which for the two WENO types is *not* the WENO
interpolant but the linear centred polynomial of the same width: `weno3` pairs with `cp3` and `weno5` with
`cp5`, selected by the last character of the module name at [`interpolation.cpp:21-36`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interpolation.cpp#L21-L36). No source in
the repository gives a rationale for that pairing, so this section records it as a design choice rather than a
derived result; the consequence is that under `weno5` the velocity and pressure face states are fifth-order
linear and are not limited, while density and tracers are.

Second, a smoothness switch replaces the split entirely. With `shock: true` every row takes `interp1` and the
floors are skipped, at `shock` ([`reconstruct.cpp:99-102`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L99-L102)), so the whole state is limited by the same
nonlinear interpolant.

### Numerical method

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-framework-map
#| fig-cap: "What a reconstruction writes, and which rows take which interpolant. (a) The face index map: interior cells are plain, ghost cells are hatched in light reddish purple, and the orange triangles are the first and last face the solver reads; the dummy faces outside that range are filled by replication, not by the interpolant. (b) The row split with shock false: density and tracers take interp1 (green), velocity and pressure take interp2 (blue). With shock true every row takes interp1."
#| fig-alt: "Left: a row of six cells, the outer two hatched, with two orange triangles marking the first and last face read. Right: four row names with arrows to either interp1 or interp2."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch04.fig_recon_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

`forward` at [`reconstruct.cpp:79-158`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L79-L158) allocates a tensor with a leading axis of two, the left and
right face states, and fills it row group by row group. The number of ghost cells the interpolant needs is read
from its own stencil width at `nghost` ([`reconstruct.cpp:86`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L86)), which sets the interior range; a block too thin
for the stencil fails the check on the next line rather than silently reading a ghost.

The writing itself is `_apply_inplace` at [`reconstruct.cpp:50-65`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L50-L65). Its index map is the part worth
reading twice: the right state of face $f$ and the left state of face $f$ come from cells on opposite sides, so
the two output slices are offset by one, and the faces outside the interior range are filled by replicating the
nearest computed face rather than by running the interpolant on ghost data.

The floors are applied after each group and they come from the equation of state options, not from the
reconstruct options: density at `density_floor` ([`reconstruct.cpp:135-137`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L135-L137)), pressure at
[`reconstruct.cpp:143-145`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L143-L145). The tracer clamp at `clamp_min_` ([`reconstruct.cpp:153-155`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L153-L155)) is different
in kind: it is applied whenever the limiter is on, *even when the caller passed `floor = false`*, so the
well-balanced path of chapter 5 that asks for no floors still gets its tracers clamped at zero.

### Tests

| test | asserts | tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_plm.cpp` | a constant field is reconstructed exactly, for `dc`, `plm` and `weno5` in all three directions | allclose defaults |
| this chapter's check | `[C1]`-`[C7]` the interpolant weights and their measured orders | round-off and fitted orders |

: Tests of the reconstruction framework. {#tbl-ch04-framework-tests}

No test covers the row split itself: that density and tracers take `interp1` while velocity and pressure take
`interp2` is asserted nowhere, and a swap would be caught only by an accuracy test.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The interpolant weights are fixed rationals for a uniform mesh. On a stretched $x_1$ grid they are applied
  unchanged, so the nominal order is not attained there.
- The programmatic default for `shock` and the YAML default disagree: the options object defaults it true while
  `from_yaml` writes false. Construction from Python and from a deck give different schemes unless the key is
  set explicitly.
:::

1. **Dead members.** The options object carries `density_floor`, `pressure_floor`, `limiter` and the two
   boundary flags, and `forward` reads none of them: the floors come from the equation of state. The report
   of the options object prints them anyway, which is misleading rather than wrong.
2. **A disabled branch.** `is_boundary_lower` ([`reconstruct.cpp:104-127`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L104-L127)) is a commented-out block that would have
   narrowed the interior range next to a physical boundary before reconstructing velocity and pressure. It is
   not compiled, and nothing in the repository records why it was switched off. Reading the file without
   noticing that it is inside a comment is an easy mistake.
3. **`scale: true`.** The key is parsed and passed to the interpolant, and issue #275 reports that setting it
   changes results in moist bubble decks through the well-balanced reference. Why it does is not explained in
   any source; this section records it as an open question rather than a mechanism.
